title: Understand Avoidance and Safety Habits
learningGoals: Notice what a habit does for you

deeperExplanation.question: Is choosing another word always avoidance?
deeperExplanation.answer: No. People change wording for clarity, accuracy, politeness and ordinary preference. The same action can serve different purposes. Ask whether you chose the wording you wanted or felt compelled to escape something at the cost of your meaning. You do not need to classify every synonym in real time. A few bounded reflections can help you recognise a pattern without turning normal language into another thing to inspect.

sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring Understand Avoidance and Safety Habits. You know the word you want, but choose another because it seems safer. Or you always start with a filler, rehearse a greeting or wait for someone else to order. The habit helps in the moment but may limit what you choose later.

In this session, we will notice what a habit does for you, explore its benefit and cost, and choose a small voluntary variation. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration: Avoidance means moving away from a speaking experience you want or need. A safety habit is something you do to feel protected while participating. A behaviour cannot be classified just by looking at it: a pause can be natural, a useful tool or a way to postpone a feared word. We will ask what the action is doing for you.

sections.narration:
You know the word you want, but choose another because it seems safer. Or you always start with a filler, rehearse a greeting or wait for someone else to order. The habit helps in the moment but may limit what you choose later.

These habits often developed for understandable reasons. Blaming them is not useful. Instead, notice their immediate benefit and longer-term cost. A support remains helpful when you can choose it flexibly. If it begins to decide every situation, you may want to explore a small alternative in a setting you choose.

sections.narration: You do not have to remove every habit, use every feared word or expose yourself publicly. The aim is greater choice over time. Ordinary language variation is not automatically avoidance. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: Notice one habit in a real exchange and decide consciously whether to use it. A deliberate choice is useful information. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
